**1 — Scene:** A portion of vegetable-topped pizza with a small piece of browned chicken and an onion-and-herb garnish.

**2 — Vessel:** A large, rounded-square dinner plate, partially cropped. I estimate its usable area as equivalent to a **26 cm round plate**: 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Pizza with melted cheese, tomato sauce, red pepper, green chili, olives, and some onion; browned chicken; a small garnish of red onion, spring onion, and herbs. Any cooking oil retained on the chicken is included in its energy estimate rather than counted separately.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area | Height | Gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pizza, including toppings | 31% | 165 cm² | 1.1 cm | 181 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 163 g | 260 | 424 kcal |
| Browned chicken | 12% | 64 cm² | 1.5 cm | 96 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 91 g | 220 | 200 kcal |
| Onion and herb garnish | 1% | 5 cm² | 0.6 cm | 3 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 2 g | 35 | 1 kcal |

The allocated areas total **44% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial empty space. Garnish overlapping the chicken is accounted for within this approximate allocation.

**8 — Sanity check:** About **256 g and 625 kcal** is plausible for the visible pizza portion and small chicken piece. The main uncertainties are the pizza thickness and the chicken’s cut and cooking fat.
